instructions: Ambiguity hunt. Choose the answer labels, then argue the strongest case for one wrong option in case {label, text}. Set flag to one sentence when that case is defensible or a constraint is missing, else null.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Administrators in member accounts have full permissions in their own accounts. The company must ensure that no one in a member account, including the root user, can turn off S3 Block Public Access at the account level. The company must also find every S3 bucket that has server access logging turned off, including buckets that already have it off today, and must turn logging back on automatically. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Attach an SCP to the organization root that denies the action that changes the account-level S3 Block Public Access settings.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an AWS Config rule that checks server access logging on each bucket, with automatic remediation through a Systems Manager Automation document.

options.label: C
options.text: Write an AWS Lambda function that runs every hour, checks the logging setting of every bucket, and turns logging on where it is off.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an AWS Config rule in proactive mode that blocks any change to the account-level S3 Block Public Access settings.

options.label: E
options.text: Enable Amazon GuardDuty in every member account, and use an Amazon EventBridge rule to turn logging back on when a finding arrives.
